lessons.title: What is a Parameter?
lessons.content: A parameter is a value you give to a function, like a name to say hello.

lessons.title: Making a Function
lessons.content: Use def and a parameter, like def say(name): to print a name.

lessons.title: Make a function say(name) to print 'Hi, ' + name.
Calling Functions
lessons.content: Call with a value, like say('Alex') to use 'Alex' as the name.

lessons.title: Using Parameters
lessons.content: The parameter acts like a variable inside the function.

lessons.title: Make a function add(a, b) to print the sum of a and b.
Parameter Names
lessons.content: Choose clear names like 'name' or 'num' for parameters.

lessons.instruction: Define a function with parameter item.

lessons.question: Can you call a function with different values?

lessons.title: Why Parameters?
lessons.content: Parameters make functions work with different data.

lessons.title: Function Star! 🌟
lessons.content: You’re using parameters like a pro! Your functions are super flexible!

lessons.title: Number Parameters
lessons.content: Functions can take numbers, like def double(num): to multiply by 2.

lessons.question: What can a function parameter be?

lessons.title: Math in Functions
lessons.content: Use numbers in functions, like def add_five(x): print(x + 5).

lessons.title: Make a function double(num) to print num * 2.
Calling with Numbers
lessons.content: Call with a number, like double(3) to use 3 as num.

lessons.question: What does double(2) print if it does num * 2?

lessons.title: Number Operations
lessons.content: Use +, -, *, / with number parameters in functions.

lessons.title: Make a function add_ten(x) to print x + 10.
Simple Calculations
lessons.content: Keep math simple in functions for easy coding.

lessons.instruction: Add 3 to num in the function.

lessons.question: Can a function use math with parameters?

lessons.title: Number Power
lessons.content: Number parameters let functions do math easily.

lessons.title: Number Function Hero! ➕
lessons.content: You’re doing math in functions! Your code is getting powerful!

lessons.title: What is Adding to Lists?
lessons.content: You can add items to a list using .append(), like list.append('new').

lessons.title: Using Append
lessons.content: Append adds an item to the end, like colors.append('red').

lessons.title: Add 'blue' to ['red'] and print the list.
Adding Any Item
lessons.content: Append can add text, numbers, or more, like list.append(5).

lessons.title: Growing Lists
lessons.content: You can append many times to make a list bigger.

lessons.title: Checking Lists
lessons.content: Print the list after appending to see the new items.

lessons.question: Where does append add an item?

lessons.title: List Growth
lessons.content: Appending makes lists useful for collecting data.

lessons.title: List Builder! 📋
lessons.content: You’re growing lists like a champ! Appending makes your code awesome!

lessons.title: What is Removing?
lessons.content: You can remove items from a list using .remove(), like list.remove('old').

lessons.title: Using Remove
lessons.content: Remove deletes the first matching item, like colors.remove('red').

lessons.title: Removing Numbers
lessons.content: Remove works with numbers too, like nums.remove(5).

lessons.title: Checking After Remove
lessons.content: Print the list after removing to see what’s left.

lessons.title: One at a Time
lessons.content: Remove deletes only the first match, not all.

lessons.question: Does remove delete all matching items?

lessons.title: List Cleanup
lessons.content: Removing helps keep lists tidy and relevant.

lessons.title: List Cleaner! 🧹
lessons.content: You’re tidying lists like a pro! Removing makes your code sharp!

lessons.title: What are Dictionaries?
lessons.content: Dictionaries store pairs, like {'name': 'Mia'} to link 'name' to 'Mia'.

lessons.title: Making Dictionaries
lessons.content: Use {}, like info = {'age': 10} to store data.

lessons.title: Getting Values
lessons.content: Use the key, like info['age'] to get 10.

lessons.title: Changing Values
lessons.content: Update with the key, like dict['key'] = 'new'.

lessons.title: Adding Pairs
lessons.content: Add new pairs, like dict['new'] = 'value'.

lessons.question: Can you add new pairs to a dictionary?

lessons.title: Dictionary Use
lessons.content: Dictionaries help organize data with keys and values.

lessons.title: Dictionary Pro! 📖
lessons.content: You’re organizing data like a wizard! Dictionaries make your code neat!

lessons.title: What is Text Case?
lessons.content: Text case changes letters, like .upper() to make 'hi' into 'HI'.

lessons.title: Using Upper
lessons.content: Use .upper(), like 'hello'.upper() to get 'HELLO'.

lessons.title: Using Lower
lessons.content: Use .lower(), like 'HI'.lower() to get 'hi'.

lessons.title: Saving Results
lessons.content: Store the result, like new = text.upper(), to use later.

lessons.title: Case Uses
lessons.content: Upper and lower help make text look right.

lessons.title: Text Case Power
lessons.content: Changing case makes text clear and professional.

lessons.title: Case Changer! 📜
lessons.content: You’re shaping text like a pro! Upper and lower make your code shine!

lessons.title: What is Replacing?
lessons.content: Replacing swaps text, like .replace('old', 'new') to change words.

lessons.title: Using Replace
lessons.content: 'cat'.replace('c', 'h') makes 'hat'.

lessons.title: Replacing Words
lessons.content: Replace whole words, like 'hi'.replace('hi', 'hello').

lessons.title: Saving Replacements
lessons.content: Store the result, like new = text.replace('a', 'b').

lessons.title: Replace 'bad' with 'good' in 'Feeling bad' and print.
Replace Uses
lessons.content: Replace fixes text or changes messages easily.

lessons.question: Does replace change the original text?

lessons.title: Replace Power
lessons.content: Replacing makes text flexible and fun to edit.

lessons.title: Replace Rockstar! 🔄
lessons.content: You’re swapping text like a pro! Replace makes your code creative!

lessons.title: What is Counting?
lessons.content: Use .count() to find how many times an item appears, like list.count('x').

lessons.title: Using Count
lessons.content: ['a', 'a'].count('a') returns 2 because 'a' appears twice.

lessons.title: Counting Numbers
lessons.content: Count numbers too, like [1, 1, 2].count(1) returns 2.

lessons.title: Saving Counts
lessons.content: Store the count, like num = list.count(3), to use it.

lessons.title: When to Count
lessons.content: Count helps check how often something appears.

lessons.title: Counting Power
lessons.content: Counting helps you understand your list data.

lessons.title: Counting Champ! 🔢
lessons.content: You’re counting items like a pro! Your lists are under control!

lessons.title: What is Elif?
lessons.content: Elif checks another condition if the first if is false, like elif x > 5:.

lessons.title: Using Elif
lessons.content: Use after if, like if x > 10: print('Big') elif x > 5: print('Medium').

lessons.title: If x = 7, print 'Medium' if >5, else 'Small'.
Multiple Elifs
lessons.content: Add more elifs for more checks, like elif x > 3:.

lessons.starterCode:
x = 3
if x > 5:
    print('Big')
 x > 2:
    print('OK')

lessons.title: With Else
lessons.content: Use else for all other cases after if and elif.

lessons.title: If x = 1, print 'Big' if >5, 'OK' if >2, else 'Tiny'.
Order Matters
lessons.content: Python checks if, then elif, then else, in order.

lessons.starterCode:
y = 8
if y > 20:
    print('High')
 y < 10:
    print('Low')

lessons.title: Conditional Power
lessons.content: Elif makes your program choose between many options.

lessons.title: Conditional King! ✅
lessons.content: You’re making choices like a pro! Elif makes your code smart!

lessons.title: What is Range?
lessons.content: Range makes numbers, like range(3) gives 0, 1, 2 for looping.

lessons.title: Using Range
lessons.content: Use in loops, like for i in range(3): print(i) to print 0, 1, 2.

lessons.title: Range in Loops
lessons.content: Range helps repeat code a set number of times.

lessons.title: Doing Things
lessons.content: Use range to print messages or do math in loops.

lessons.title: Range Numbers
lessons.content: Range always starts at 0 and stops before the number.

lessons.question: What is the last number in range(4)?

lessons.title: Range Power
lessons.content: Range makes looping easy and fun for beginners.

lessons.title: Range Ruler! 🔢
lessons.content: You’re looping with range like a pro! Your code is repeating perfectly!

lessons.title: What is Combining?
lessons.content: Use + to join lists, like ['a'] + ['b'] makes ['a', 'b'].

lessons.title: Using +
lessons.content: Add lists, like list1 + list2 to make one big list.

lessons.title: Saving Combined Lists
lessons.content: Store the result, like new = list1 + list2.

lessons.title: Combining More Lists
lessons.content: You can join many lists, like list1 + list2 + list3.

lessons.title: List Order
lessons.content: The first list’s items come first in the result.

lessons.title: Combine Power
lessons.content: Combining lists helps collect data together.

lessons.title: List Combiner! 🔗
lessons.content: You’re joining lists like a pro! Your code is building big lists!

lessons.title: What is Checking?
lessons.content: Use 'in' to check if an item is in a list, like 'x' in ['x', 'y'].

lessons.title: Using In
lessons.content: 'cat' in ['cat', 'dog'] returns True if 'cat' is there.

lessons.title: With If
lessons.content: Use 'in' with if, like if 'x' in list: print('Found').

lessons.title: Checking Uses
lessons.content: Checking helps find items before using them.

lessons.title: Check if 'dog' is in ['cat'] and print 'Found' if true.
True or False
lessons.content: 'in' returns True if the item is found, False if not.

lessons.title: Check Power
lessons.content: Checking makes sure your program uses the right data.

lessons.title: Check Champion! 🔍
lessons.content: You’re finding items like a pro! Checking keeps your code accurate!

lessons.title: What is a While Loop?
lessons.content: A while loop repeats while a condition is true, like while x < 3:.

lessons.question: When does a while loop run?

lessons.title: Writing While
lessons.content: Use while, like while count < 3: print(count), and change count.

lessons.title: Changing Variables
lessons.content: Update the variable, like count += 1, to stop the loop.

lessons.instruction: Add 1 to x in the loop.

lessons.title: Simple Loops
lessons.content: Keep while loops simple to avoid mistakes.

lessons.title: Loop End
lessons.content: The loop stops when the condition is false.

lessons.title: While Power
lessons.content: While loops repeat tasks until you want them to stop.

lessons.title: While Wizard! 🔄
lessons.content: You’re looping like a pro! While loops make your code repeat easily!

lessons.title: What is Comparing?
lessons.content: Compare numbers with >, <, ==, like x > y to check if x is bigger.

lessons.title: Using Comparisons
lessons.content: Use in if, like if x > 5: print('Big') to compare.

lessons.title: Equal Check
lessons.content: Use == to check if numbers are the same, like x == 5.

lessons.title: Less Than
lessons.content: Use < to check if a number is smaller, like x < 10.

lessons.title: Comparison Results
lessons.content: Comparisons give True or False to help make choices.

lessons.title: Comparison Power
lessons.content: Comparing helps your program make smart decisions.

lessons.title: Comparison Captain! ⚖️
lessons.content: You’re comparing numbers like a pro! Your code is making choices!

lessons.title: What is Counting?
lessons.content: Counting tracks how many times something happens, like in a loop.

lessons.title: Using a Counter
lessons.content: Use a variable, like count = 0, and add 1 each time.

lessons.title: Count from 1 to 3 in a loop.
lessons.expectedAnswer:
count = 0
for i in range(3):
    count += 1
print(count)

lessons.title: Counting in While
lessons.content: Use while to count, like while x < 3: x += 1.

lessons.title: Counting Items
lessons.content: Count specific items, like how many 5s in a list.

lessons.title: Count 1s in [1, 2, 1].
Saving Counts
lessons.content: Store the count in a variable to use later.

count = 0
for i in range(2):
     += 1
print(count)

lessons.title: Counting Power
lessons.content: Counting helps track data in your programs.

lessons.title: Counting Genius! 🧮
lessons.content: You’re counting like a pro! Your code is keeping track perfectly!
